description: An operations director must decide whether to authorize a controller-firmware retrofit on Welding Cell 5 before its next production run and finalize the downtime, production recovery, and post-change quality controls, with input from controls engineering, production planning, and quality.

shared_context.S1: Welding Cell 5 uses a controller firmware version that will reach the end of vendor support this month.
shared_context.S2: A firmware retrofit for Welding Cell 5 is tentatively scheduled for Friday before the cell's next production run.
shared_context.S3: The Friday customer order requires 240 finished assemblies from the Welding Cell 5 production family.
shared_context.S4: At the Friday 08:00 change-control huddle, Elena asks controls engineering, production planning, and quality to report any relevant requirements before authorizing the work.
shared_context.S5: The huddle's closeout routine is for Elena to make the authorization decision after each function has reported and to record follow-up actions for later scheduling or documentation; missing cycle-time or validation-duration estimates are not prerequisites for closing this authorization decision.

PF1.text: Ravi confirmed with the controller vendor yesterday that a safety bulletin identifies an interlock race in the current firmware; the retrofit must be completed before Welding Cell 5's next production run, and the work requires exactly 6 hours of energized lockout and post-update safety-I/O validation. The vendor bulletin has not yet been attached to the work order.

PF2.text: Marta's production-capacity check shows that alternate Welding Cell 4 can produce exactly 160 of the 240 assemblies by Friday 16:00; the remaining exactly 80 assemblies must be produced on Cell 5 after the retrofit, and the Cell 4 reservation expires Thursday at noon. She has not entered the temporary reservation in the production system.

PF3.text: Jonah verified in the customer's quality portal that exactly the first 20 assemblies made after a controller change must be held for weld-macro and dimensional validation before release. The customer requirement has not yet been copied into the local inspection plan.

acceptance_conditions: The firmware retrofit must be authorized before the next Welding Cell 5 production run.
The retrofit plan must reserve exactly 6 hours for energized lockout and post-update safety-I/O validation.
Exactly 160 assemblies must be assigned to alternate Welding Cell 4.
Exactly 80 assemblies must be assigned to Welding Cell 5 after the retrofit.
Exactly the first 20 post-retrofit assemblies must be held for weld-macro and dimensional validation before release.
A safety-I/O or retrofit documentation commitment and a post-change quality-validation commitment must be recorded.
The vendor safety bulletin must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] in ['documentation', 'safety_io_validation', 'schedule'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] in ['quality_plan_update', 'quality_hold', 'post_change_quality_validation'] for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The safety bulletin changes authorization from a discretionary support upgrade to a required pre-run retrofit, sets the lockout and validation duration at exactly 6 hours, and requires a retrofit-related documentation or execution commitment.
The capacity check changes the recovery allocation to exactly 160 assemblies on Cell 4 and exactly 80 assemblies on Cell 5 after the retrofit.
The customer portal requirement changes the release plan to a hold of exactly the first 20 post-change assemblies and requires a recorded quality-hold or inspection-plan commitment.
